prerequisites: Secondary education mathematics with at least 6 hours of mathematics lessons.

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows the concepts from higher-dimensional linear algebra: vector spaces, linear dependence, orthogonality.
The student can characterize matrices based on their elementary spaces, rank, determinant, eigenvalues; the student knows and understands the relationships between these.
The student recognizes linear transformations between vector spaces and can describe them mathematically and perform operations on them (composition, inversion).
The student can recognize and solve least squares problems.
The student can factorize a matrix.
The student can perform calculations with complex numbers: addition, multiplication, exponentiation.
The student understands formal proofs of theorems in algebra.

The student can convert some engineering problems into an algebraic representation: setting up a system of linear equations, processing measurement data, analyzing autonomous systems and vibrations as an eigenvalue problem, calculating the response of linear time-invariant discrete-time systems, dimension reduction with singular value decomposition.
The student can use Matlab to perform elementary matrix operations.

syllabus_topics: Systems of linear equations, matrix and solution set
Linear transformations from R^n to R^m
Sum of matrices, product with a scalar, product of matrices
Inverse of a square matrix and invertibility theorems
Linear mappings, null space, column space
Dimension, rank, row space, dimension theorem
Application to dynamic systems in discrete time: stability, response
Inner product, length, orthogonality in R^n
Application: processing measurements in a linear model
Vector spaces equipped with an inner product, Cauchy-Schwartz inequality
Diagonalization of symmetric matrices, spectral decomposition
Singular value decomposition: calculation and interpretation
Pseudo-inverse and relation to least squares
assessment_rules: A mid-term test is organized. If the student passes the mid-term test and achieves a better result on it than on the exam during the next examination period, the mid-term test result will be factored into the final result for that period, with a weighting of one-fourth for the mid-term test and three-fourths for the exam. This recalculation does not apply to results obtained in the third examination period. The main exam consists of two parts: a written exam (75% of the grade) and a PC-lab exercise using Matlab (25% of the grade). Both parts of the exam must be retaken if the student fails; there is no recalculation of mid-term test scores for resits.
